payload.source_label: Solve linear hyperbolic Riemann data using eigenvalues and eigenvectors of A

contract.statement: For the constant-coefficient real linear system q_t + A q_x = 0, hyperbolicity means that A has real eigenvalues and a complete eigenvector basis (printed pp. 1 and 3). With constant left and right initial states separated at x = 0 as in (1.11), the source asserts that the Riemann problem can be solved using the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of A, referring the construction to Chapter 3 (printed pp. 5–6). The surrounding text describes hyperbolic Riemann solutions as typically depending on x/t and comprising finitely many waves with constant propagation speeds (printed p. 5); the eigenvalues give the linear wave speeds (printed p. 3). The supplied passage leaves the interface values, precise discontinuous-solution formulation, and detailed spectral construction unspecified (printed p. 5, opening paragraph and section 1.2.1; printed p. 6, continuation).
assumptions: The system is q_t + A q_x = 0 with A constant and real. [Printed p. 1, (1.1).]
The system is hyperbolic: A has real eigenvalues and m linearly independent corresponding eigenvectors. [Printed p. 3, opening paragraph.]
The initial data have the Riemann form q(x,0) = q_l for x < 0 and q(x,0) = q_r for x > 0, placing the interface at the origin. [Printed p. 5, section 1.2.1, (1.11).]

The selected linear Riemann assertion inherits its equation, state space, and matrix assumptions from (1.1), and its meaning of hyperbolicity from the opening paragraph of printed page 3. [Printed p. 1, (1.1); printed p. 3, opening paragraph; printed pp. 5–6, linear Riemann sentence.]

Discontinuous solutions are not required to satisfy the differential equation classically at their discontinuities; the surrounding text instead invokes integral conservation. The actual formula (1.10) is not present in the supplied images. [Printed p. 5, opening paragraph.]

The finite-volume application supplies q_l and q_r from adjacent cell averages, but this is introduced conditionally as an application, not as a restriction on the definition of Riemann data. [Printed p. 5, paragraph following (1.11).]

Chapter 3 is explicitly cited for the linear solution construction. Its contents were not supplied among the allowed page images, so no detailed Chapter 3 formula is included in this extraction. [Printed pp. 5–6, sentence spanning the page break.]
quantifiers: Inherited setting: a component count m and a constant real matrix A of size m × m; the passage does not explicitly quantify the permissible values of m. [Printed p. 1, equation (1.1) and following paragraph.]
Unknown state q : R × R → R^m, with spatial variable x and time variable t. [Printed p. 1, paragraph following (1.1).]

Left and right constant states q_l and q_r, taking values in the state space R^m when (1.11) is applied to system (1.1). Their state-space typing is inherited from q. [Printed p. 1, (1.1); printed p. 5, (1.11).]
Real eigenvalues and a corresponding complete set of m eigenvectors of A; no eigenvalue ordering or eigenvector normalization is specified. [Printed p. 3, opening paragraph.]
